```{r setup}
library(bdhs)
```

## Why bdhs does not ship the microdata

The DHS Program gives respondent-level data free of charge to registered
researchers. Its terms of use say the data must not be passed on to others or
redistributed "directly or within any tool". So bdhs never bundles, uploads or
shares microdata, and you should keep your files somewhere private: not in a
public GitHub repository and preferably not in a synced cloud folder.

Getting access is quick:

1. Create an account at
   <https://dhsprogram.com/data/new-user-registration.cfm>.
2. Describe your research project and request the Bangladesh surveys.
3. Once approved, download the datasets. The **Stata** format (`.DTA`, in
   files like `BDIR81DT.ZIP`) is recommended because it keeps all variable and
   value labels.

Analyses published from BDHS data must cite the survey's final report. The
Bangladesh conditions of use also ask for a copy of each publication to be
sent to the NIPORT library.

## What exists

`bdhs_inventory()` lists every dataset the DHS Program distributes for
Bangladesh and marks which ones you already have:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
bdhs_inventory()
```

The main recode files are:

```{r}
bdhs_recodes()[1:10, ]
```

Not every recode exists for every round. For example, men were last
interviewed in 2011, and the pregnancy (`GR`) and postnatal care (`NR`)
recodes are new in 2022.

## Importing your downloads

Point `bdhs_import()` at the files, zips or folders you downloaded.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
bdhs_import("~/Downloads/BDHS")
```

`bdhs_import()` does the following:

* Recognises DHS files by name (`BDIR81FL.DTA`), inside zips (`BDIR81DT.ZIP`),
  with prefixes (`2022BDPR81FL.DTA`), and even when you renamed them
  (`BDHS2018KR.DTA`). In that case it checks the file's contents.
* Skips files that are not original DHS recodes, such as your own merged or
  appended datasets.
* Stores a fast copy in the bdhs data directory. With the arrow package
  installed this is a column-oriented copy, so reading a few variables from a
  5,000-column file is quick. Use `copy = FALSE` to leave files where they are
  and only register them.
* Warns if the data directory is inside a git repository or a cloud-sync
  folder.

The data directory defaults to `tools::R_user_dir("bdhs", "data")`. Use
`bdhs_data_dir("path")` to change it for the session, or set the
`BDHS_DATA_DIR` environment variable in your `.Renviron` to change it for good.
`bdhs_sitrep()` summarises your setup.

## A complete example with synthetic files

The chunk below runs the full workflow on synthetic files written to a
temporary folder, so you can see each step without real data.

```{r}
# A temporary data directory and some fake DHS files
old <- Sys.getenv("BDHS_DATA_DIR")
store <- file.path(tempdir(), "bdhs-store")
Sys.setenv(BDHS_DATA_DIR = store)

downloads <- file.path(tempdir(), "downloads")
dir.create(downloads, showWarnings = FALSE)
haven::write_dta(bdhs_simulate(2022, "IR"), file.path(downloads, "BDIR81FL.DTA"))
haven::write_dta(bdhs_simulate(2022, "KR"), file.path(downloads, "BDKR81FL.DTA"))
haven::write_dta(bdhs_simulate(2017, "HR"), file.path(downloads, "BDHS2018HR.DTA"))
```

```{r}
bdhs_import(downloads)
```

```{r}
ir <- bdhs_read(2022, "IR", vars = c("v012", "v106", "v313"))
ir
attr(ir, "bdhs_survey_id")
```

When you ask for specific variables, `bdhs_read()` always adds the identifiers
and design variables (cluster, strata, weight, region, residence and the
all-woman factors). That way the result can go straight into `bdhs_design()`
or `bdhs_merge()`. Use `labels = "factor"` to get factors instead of labelled
numbers.

```{r, include = FALSE}
Sys.setenv(BDHS_DATA_DIR = old)
```

## Downloading with your DHS account (experimental)

`bdhs_download()` can log in to the DHS website with **your** account and
fetch files directly:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
bdhs_download(2022, c("IR", "KR"), email = "you@university.edu", project = "Your project title")
```

Your password is never stored by bdhs. It is read from the system keyring
(keyring package, service `"bdhs-dhs"`), the `DHS_PASSWORD` environment
variable, or an interactive prompt. The DHS website can change without
notice, so if the downloader fails, download the files in your browser and use
`bdhs_import()`.

## Reading one-off files

`bdhs_read_file()` reads any DHS file without registering it and applies the
same conventions: lower-case names, preserved labels and detected survey and
recode.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pr <- bdhs_read_file("~/Downloads/BDPR81FL.DTA", vars = c("hv104", "hv105"))
```
